rules: LESSONS L1-L15: no music bed, a line within 0.5 s, the trouble clear by 3 s, one key line on screen, nothing after the peak.

scripts.title: The Last Guy
scripts.observation: Every tradesperson breathes in through their teeth at the last person's work, and it is never their own.
scripts.caption_question: Who did this to you?
scripts.new: a dripping pipe under the sink, a yellow invoice insert, a business card insert

beats.picture: Held frame: Rex's head out from under the sink, torch in mouth taken away. A slow drip beside him. Fern, arms folded.
lines: Oh, no. Who did this to you?
beats.sound: long breath in through teeth, drip

beats.picture: He shines the torch back under. The drip quickens.
lines: A child did this. A child, in the dark.
Whoever did this should not own a wrench.

beats.picture: He takes a photo of the pipe with his phone.
lines: I'm sending this to the guys. They'll want to see this.

beats.picture: Fern lays a yellow invoice on the floor beside him. Insert: REX'S PLUMBING, March, signed Rex.
Rex looks at it. Looks at the pipe. The drip lands on the invoice.
He wipes his paws and slides a card across the floor. Insert: REX. WE FIX WHAT THE LAST GUY DID.
Fern's face, not moving. The pipe gives a small spray behind her.

scripts.title: Wave Back
scripts.observation: You wave back at someone who was waving at the person behind you, then your arm has to become something else.
scripts.caption_question: Ever waved back at someone who wasn't waving at you?
scripts.new: none

beats.picture: Noor walking, a man ahead throws up an arm and grins. She beams and waves back, arm high.
He walks straight past her and hugs someone behind her. Her arm stays up.
She slowly turns the wave into a stretch, for nobody.
A passer-by stops and copies her.
Same sidewalk: six people stretching in rows behind her.
Card: THREE YEARS LATER. Her gym, a poster: STRETCH WITH NOOR. She wears a headset at the desk.
The same man comes through the door, sees her, and waves. She checks behind her. Nobody there. She looks back. Her arm stays down.
His arm stays up. He slowly turns it into a stretch.

scripts.title: You Have It
scripts.observation: Nobody will eat the last slice, but everyone will eat half of what is left of it.
scripts.caption_question: Who eats the last slice?
scripts.new: a slice of cake in halving sizes, tweezers

beats.picture: Held frame: two friends, one plate, one slice of cake between them. Neither blinks.
Priya takes the knife, cuts it in half, eats one half. The plate goes back to the middle.
Deb cuts what is left in half and eats it. Smaller each time.
Deb takes out tweezers. Priya holds her breath. A crumb is parted.
A speck on the plate. Priya lowers the point of a pin onto it. Silence.
A tiny ping. A hum. The pendant lamps dim. The window goes white. The whole frame blows back.
beats.sound: ping, rising hum, a huge muffled boom

beats.picture: Smoke clears: hair blown flat, soot on both faces, table gone, plate still in Priya's hand, the speck still on it.
beats.camera: hold on the two of them

scripts.title: How Is Everything
scripts.observation: The waiter only ever asks how everything is at the second your mouth is full.
scripts.caption_question: How does the waiter always know?
scripts.new: a sandwich, a paper napkin

beats.picture: Milo bites a sandwich. Ava is instantly at his elbow.
She is gone. He chews, swallows, watches her wipe a far table. He lifts the sandwich slowly. Bites. She is at his elbow.
He tests her. Opens wide, bites nothing, chews air. He looks round. Nobody comes. He smiles.
He takes a real bite. She is there.
Plate empty. Mouth empty. He waves for the bill. She walks past. He calls. She looks straight through him.
He looks at the napkin. He looks at her. He puts it in his mouth and bites.
She is at his elbow. He holds up his card, chewing.
beats.sound: whip of air, card reader beep

beats.picture: She leaves with the card. He keeps chewing the napkin, eyes wet, undefeated.

scripts.title: Eye Chart
scripts.observation: At the eye test one and two look identical, and the optician's calm makes it feel like an exam on your whole life.
scripts.caption_question: Better with one, or two?
scripts.new: an eye chart whose lower rows sharpen when a lens clicks, a lens frame

beats.picture: Held frame: Deb behind a lens frame, Dr. Feld's hand on the dial, the chart a blur behind her.
Click. A row snaps sharp.
Deb frowns. Feld writes. Click. The next row sharpens.
lines: That was not... a small mistake.

beats.picture: Click. Deb's voice drops.
lines: He is not... going to change.

beats.picture: Feld, unbothered, turns the dial one last notch. The bottom row, tiny, comes clear.
Insert: YOUR MOTHER WAS RIGHT. Deb reads it. Nobody speaks.
Feld, pen ready.
lines: Can I go back to one?

beats.picture: Click. The chart melts to a blur. Deb's whole face relaxes. She smiles at nothing.
beats.sound: lens click, a small contented sigh

scripts.title: Mosquito
scripts.observation: One mosquito in a dark bedroom can defeat a grown adult at 2 a.m., and it vanishes the moment the light goes on.
scripts.caption_question: Who else has lost a night to one mosquito?
scripts.new: a mosquito speck with a wandering path, a rolled towel

beats.picture: Dark. Bruno's eyes are already open, a whine passing his ear. He says it at once, then slaps his own ear hard.
Light on: nothing. Light off: the whine is back. On: nothing. Mae, face in the pillow.
Light on: Bruno on his feet on the bed, towel rolled, breathing through his mouth.
beats.camera: low angle, wide enough for the whole body

beats.picture: He swings at the air. He slaps his forehead, then his cheek. It whines on, unharmed.
Bruno stands frozen on the bed, towel raised. The whine stops. It lands on his own forehead. His eyes cross.
Mae, face in the pillow and not waking, lifts one arm and whacks it.
beats.camera: hold on the two of them

beats.picture: He sways. She has not moved. The light clicks off. Dark. Then, faintly, one whine. His eyes open.

scripts.title: Did You Pack
scripts.observation: A grandmother hears 'I'm full' as 'more, please', and a meal follows you to the airport.
scripts.caption_question: Did you pack this bag yourself?
scripts.new: an x-ray screen insert, a foil parcel with a note

beats.picture: Held frame: Dev at the table, plate piled high, Grandma standing over him with a spoon.
Another spoonful lands.
At the door he has a coat on. She zips something into his bag.
Airport. The bag on the belt. The officer stops it.
lines: Did you pack this bag yourself?

beats.picture: Insert: x-ray: a whole chicken, a tray of lasagna, a rolling pin.
The officer opens the bag. On top, a foil parcel with a note. Insert: FOR THE MAN AT SECURITY. YOU LOOK THIN.
He looks at the note. He looks down at himself. His chin wobbles. He takes a bite and waves Dev through.

scripts.title: Sinking Chair
scripts.observation: The office chair slowly lowers you during a serious meeting, and nobody ever says a word about it.
scripts.caption_question: Has your chair ever done this in a meeting?
scripts.new: a typed chair drop on the existing cut

beats.picture: Across the desk, level with the Boss. The chair gives a sigh and he drops an inch.
He keeps his chin up. Another inch.
His shoulders reach the desk. He pulls at the lever behind him, smiling.
beats.camera: hold, the desk edge now cuts his chest

beats.picture: The Boss has not looked up from his notes.
Only his eyes and quiff clear the desk.
beats.camera: hold, low and small in the frame

beats.picture: The Boss finally looks over the edge of the desk, down at him.
lines: Three years in that chair. You've never said a word.
beats.camera: cut to the Boss, high angle

beats.picture: The Boss goes back to his notes.
lines: Your salary works the same way.

beats.picture: The last of the quiff slides below the desk. The Boss writes on.
beats.sound: one long pssht, a soft clunk
beats.camera: hold on the empty desk edge

scripts.title: Sensor
scripts.observation: Automatic taps, soap and doors do not believe you exist, and you end up waving at a sink.
scripts.caption_question: Why do automatic taps ignore you?
scripts.new: a sensor tap, a soap dispenser and a hand dryer on the existing wall

beats.picture: Held frame: Jun at a sink, both hands up, frozen mid-wave under a dry tap.
He tries the soap: nothing. The dryer: nothing. He jumps. The light clicks off. He waves in the dark. It clicks on.
At the next sink, not looking up, Omar waves one slow hand, the wave of a man with a routine.
beats.camera: reveal: a move right onto Omar

beats.picture: Jun laughs.
lines: How long have you been in here?

beats.picture: Omar keeps waving.
lines: I came in to wash my hands in 1987.

beats.picture: Jun goes to the door. It does not open. He waves at it. Then Kai walks in. Tap on. Soap. Dryer. Door opens by itself as he leaves.
beats.camera: wide, no cut during the gag

beats.picture: The door shuts one inch from Jun's fingers. Silence. Omar has not turned.

scripts.title: Fitted Sheet
scripts.observation: No adult can fold a fitted sheet, and everyone privately believes they are the only one who just balls it up.
scripts.key_line: How do you fold a fitted sheet?
scripts.caption_question: How do you fold a fitted sheet?
scripts.new: a padlock and key on the closet, balled sheets, a perfectly square folded sheet

beats.picture: Mae wrestling a sheet, arms lost in it, her mother (the hedgehog) passing behind her.
lines: Mom, how do you fold a fitted sheet?

beats.picture: Her mother stops dead. She shuts the door behind them, very quietly.
Her mother draws a key from round her neck.
lines: My mother showed me. Her mother showed her.

beats.picture: The closet: neat folded towels in front, a padlock. She turns the key. Hold.
The door opens. Balled sheets roll out, then pour out, burying Mae to the waist. Her mother stands in them, serene.
lines: We ball it up. We shove it in.

beats.picture: Mae, whispering, sheets to her waist.
lines: Every woman you have ever met.
beats.camera: hold on the two of them

beats.picture: The door opens. Bruno, cheerful, holds a perfectly square folded sheet.
Both women slowly turn.

scripts.title: Seat Belt Sign
scripts.observation: The plane lands and everyone stands up to wait, bent under the bins, for twenty minutes.
scripts.caption_question: Why does everyone stand up when the plane lands?
scripts.new: none

beats.picture: Held frame: row 31. Noor seated with a book. Dev bent double under the bins, head on one side, neck against a stranger's bag.
He squeezes up the aisle past two people.
Row 14. A stranger's armpit at his ear. A chip reads 9 minutes.
A chip reads 16 minutes. His arm has gone. Someone's bag rests on his neck. A child stares at him from below.
A chime.
lines: Today we'll be leaving by the rear door.

beats.picture: Every head turns round. At row 31, Noor closes her book, stands, stretches and picks up her bag.
beats.camera: cut to Noor, upright, the only straight spine on board

beats.picture: Dev, at the far end of a hundred people, face in the armpit.
beats.sound: a door sighs open far behind him

scripts.title: Headphones
scripts.observation: With headphones in you have no idea how loud you are, so the whole aisle hears your private call.
scripts.caption_question: How loud are you with headphones in?
scripts.new: earbuds on Rosa, as a prop

beats.picture: Rosa wheels into frame, earbuds in, serene, shouting. Milo beside her freezes with a box in his hand.
She reads a tin.
Milo edges away. She follows the same way.
lines: I TOLD HIM. HAROLD, I SAID, THAT IS NOT A MOLE.

beats.picture: Down the aisle, other shoppers have stopped.
lines: HE WON'T SHOW THE DOCTOR. HE SHOWED THE NEIGHBORS.
beats.camera: cut wider, shelves of still people

beats.picture: Milo taps her arm and mimes the earbuds.
She takes one out. Her real voice is tiny.
She looks down the aisle at all of them. All of them look back.
The loudspeaker clicks on, soft and kind.
lines: Oatmeal baths are on aisle nine.

scripts.title: One Symptom
scripts.observation: You look up one headache at 1 a.m. and by 1:05 you are writing a will.
scripts.caption_question: Why did you look it up?
scripts.new: none

beats.picture: Held frame: the patient on the edge of the couch, phone in both hands, the doctor opposite.
lines: It's late-stage tongue rot. Eleven known cases.

beats.picture: The patient scrolls.
lines: At one in the morning. I've written a will.

beats.picture: The doctor sighs, holds out a hand, takes the phone and reads, slowly.
lines: Give me that. Headache. Dry mouth. Tingling left thumb.

beats.picture: He stops. He looks at his left thumb. It twitches. He swallows, dryly.
beats.sound: a very small click of the throat

beats.picture: He looks up.
Same room: they have swapped. The doctor on the couch with his coat on. The patient at the desk with the phone, reading from it.
lines: Four days. But there's a forum.

beats.picture: The doctor nods, very small.

scripts.title: The Tongs
scripts.observation: At a barbecue one person holds the tongs and nobody else may touch the meat.
scripts.caption_question: Who runs the grill at your family barbecue?
scripts.new: a grill, tongs, a pizza box, a sauce bottle

beats.picture: Bo clicks a pair of tongs twice at the camera, a grill smoking beside him.
He leaves for the sauce. Smoke thickens. Pip looks round, picks up the spare tongs and turns one burger. Juno, on the bench with her phone, does not look up.
Bo is back. The lawn goes silent. A bird stops.
Standoff across the grill, tongs at hip height.
Bo reaches slowly behind his back and draws a second pair of tongs.
They circle. Behind them the burgers turn black and the flames rise. Juno walks in between them with a flat box from the gate.
beats.sound: a car door, a far dog

beats.picture: Both tongs droop. Pip walks to the box. Bo's tongs come down gently on the lid.

scripts.title: First Sip
scripts.observation: The waiter pours a little and you swirl and nod as if you could tell, and everyone at the table lets you.
scripts.caption_question: Can anyone actually taste the difference?
scripts.new: a wine glass, a water jug

beats.picture: Held frame: Brent's nose deep in a glass, eyes shut. Omar stands by, white cloth over his arm. Deb watches.
He swirls it. Some goes on the cloth.
He sips and gargles softly. Holds up a finger.
He offers her the glass. She sips.
He leans back, a man at home in the world.
lines: Some wet dog at the end. What year?

beats.picture: Omar has not moved.
Omar tips the jug in his other hand, so it can be seen.
lines: That's the water. I was topping you up.

beats.picture: Brent looks at the glass. Deb looks at Brent. He puts it down and straightens his tie.

scripts.title: Warranty
scripts.observation: Every appliance breaks the day after its warranty ends.
scripts.caption_question: Why does it always die the day after?
scripts.reuse: soft-shovel, soft-time-card as the clock card
scripts.new: a washing machine, a brick, a bowling ball

beats.picture: Pip drops a brick into a running washing machine and slams the door. Card: 11:41.
He loads a second brick.
lines: It's going to die the second it's over. They always do. So it dies now. While it's free.

beats.picture: The machine hums, gently, perfectly. He shoves in a bowling ball.
Card: 11:56. Juno has joined him, pouring in a bag of coins, then the shovel. It purrs on.
Card: 11:59. They sit on the floor, spent, watching it. It finishes its cycle with a little tune.
Card: 12:00. A tiny click. The machine stops. A thread of smoke.
Across the room, one at a time: the lamp goes out. The TV. The fridge stops humming.
beats.camera: hold on the two of them, the room dimming

beats.picture: Near dark. A long pause.
lines: When did we buy the house?

beats.picture: A long creak overhead. Dust falls on Pip's sprout. They look up.

scripts.title: Best Day
scripts.observation: You find the spinach in your teeth at 5 p.m. and replay every smile you got that day.
scripts.caption_question: Why does nobody ever tell you?
scripts.new: a spinach leaf on the teeth

beats.picture: Held frame: Deb at the bus stop, lips closed, chin up, the only person in color with the sun on her. Her voice over it.
beats.camera: close, lips shut, the teeth not seen

beats.picture: Gary, at the stop, looks at her mouth and smiles. She smiles back, turned from the camera.
Boardroom. She presents, seen from behind. Brent cannot stop staring at her mouth.
Brent slides a napkin across the table towards her and taps his own tooth.
Bathroom, evening. She looks in the mirror, proud, and smiles her biggest smile.
beats.camera: the mirror, her face full on

beats.picture: Across both front teeth: a whole, wide leaf of spinach. Her smile stays where it is.
Same smile, tiny voice.
Next morning, bus stop. Brent arrives, beaming, a leaf across his teeth. She looks at it. She smiles at him and says nothing.

scripts.title: Bin Day
scripts.observation: You hear the bin truck from bed and run down the street in your robe while the neighbors watch.
scripts.caption_question: Who else has chased the bin truck in a robe?
scripts.new: a wheelie bin, a bin truck, a robe

beats.picture: Dev bursts out of the front door in a robe, dragging a bin. In a window above, two neighbors with mugs.
lines: And he's out of the door. Robe only.
He's left it very late, Walt.
beats.camera: medium on Dev, cut to the window

beats.picture: He runs. A slipper flies off.
lines: That's the left. He's never been strong on the left.

beats.picture: The truck pulls away. A wheel comes off the bin. He drags it, sparks.
He dives, slides, and the bin hits the back of the truck. He gets up with both arms in the air.
beats.sound: a clang, a faint cheer from an upstairs window

beats.picture: The driver leans out and looks at the bin.
The truck drives off. Dev stands in the road, one slipper, arms slowly coming down.
beats.camera: wide, Dev small in the road

beats.picture: In the window, Margaret sips.

scripts.title: Slept Wrong
scripts.observation: After forty you can be injured by sneezing, bending for a sock or sleeping, and friends trade those stories like war veterans.
scripts.key_line: Sneezed. Lost the whole left side.
scripts.caption_question: What's the stupidest way you've hurt your back?
scripts.new: none

beats.picture: Held frame: two old friends in a booth, staring into their drinks like men back from a war.
lines: Sneezed. Tuesday. Lost the whole left side.

beats.picture: The goat nods slowly.
lines: I bent down for a sock.

beats.picture: The young waiter bounces in with a tray.
lines: What happened to you guys? Rugby?

beats.picture: Nobody answers. The sloth turns his head, slowly, to the goat.
The sloth raises his glass, very slowly.
beats.sound: a far chair scrapes, as if the room had stood

beats.picture: The waiter laughs and bends to pick up a dropped napkin. A small click. He stops halfway down. He does not come back up.
beats.camera: wide on the waiter, no cut

beats.picture: Neither old friend looks round.

scripts.title: Shortest Line
scripts.observation: Whichever checkout line you pick becomes the slowest one, and switching only moves the problem with you.
scripts.caption_question: Why is the line you pick always the slowest?
scripts.new: a coin purse, a tin of peas

beats.picture: Milo slides into the shortest line, one item in hand. Rosa's cart rolls in just ahead of him.
lines: I've just got a few, dear.

beats.picture: She opens a purse and starts counting. He glances at the next lane, empty, and moves.
Rosa's cart rolls in ahead of him again.
He moves to a third lane. He looks left. Rosa is there. He looks right. She is in front of him.
She counts one coin onto the belt. Then a second, after a while.
He looks in her cart. One tin of peas.
lines: You don't need anything, do you?

beats.picture: She turns her head. The glasses catch the light.
lines: I'm seventy-nine, dear. I've got nowhere to be.

beats.picture: She leans in.
lines: I like your face when it happens.

beats.picture: She rolls on. Over her shoulder.

scripts.title: The Scale
scripts.observation: Everyone takes off shoes, belt and watch before the doctor's scale, as if a watch were the problem.
scripts.caption_question: How much does a watch weigh?
scripts.new: a doctor's scale with a height bar, shoes, a belt, a watch, keys

beats.picture: Held frame: Gary with one foot raised over a scale, frozen, a pile of nothing yet on the chair. Priya with a clipboard.
Shoes off, one at a time, and set on the chair.
Belt. He lays his watch on the pile like evidence.
Wallet. Keys. Phone. Glasses.
beats.camera: the pile grows in the corner of the frame

beats.picture: He takes out his gum and hands it to her. He breathes all the way out and steps on, leaning back.
She lowers the height bar onto his head.
He looks at her. He looks at the pile on the chair. He picks up one shoe and holds it to his chest.

scripts.title: Quiet Please
scripts.observation: Your stomach only speaks in silent rooms, and across a silent room another stomach answers.
scripts.caption_question: Why does it only happen in silent rooms?
scripts.new: a QUIET PLEASE sign, books

beats.picture: Bo, a finger to his lips, turns to the room. A silent reading room. Pip with a book, Juno far across from him.
beats.camera: medium on Bo under the sign, cut to Pip

beats.picture: Pip's belly wobbles. Bo's eyes slide over. Tinted caption, small: 'hello?'
Across the room, Juno's belly wobbles. Caption in a second tint: 'hello.' Both of them look up.
Captions, back and forth: 'he skipped breakfast' / 'she had a rice cake' / 'a what?' / 'i know'.
They hold each other's eye. A blush on each. Captions: 'are you seeing anyone?' / 'just a yogurt'.
Bo walks up between them, slowly. Finger rises.
A vast, deep growl from Bo. The table shakes. A big caption: 'HELLO.' Everyone looks at his belly.
Bo's caption: 'NOTHING SINCE TUESDAY. WHO HAS SNACKS?' Bo keeps his finger on his lips. Pip slides a yogurt along the table.

scripts.title: Some Assembly
scripts.observation: Flat-pack furniture ends with four spare screws and a review of the relationship.
scripts.caption_question: Has flat-pack furniture ever nearly ended a relationship?
scripts.new: a flat-pack wardrobe in stages, a manual with drawn steps as inserts

beats.picture: Held frame: Noor on the floor with an open manual, Dev among planks. Insert: two drawn figures, smiling.
The wardrobe half up. A door is on backwards.
Noor looks down. Insert, step 9: two figures, a speech bubble: YOU SAID YOU MEASURED. They both stare.
She turns the page. Insert, step 10: one figure, arms crossed.
Insert, step 14: one figure on a sofa. Insert, step 22: a suitcase. Noor's phone rings: MOM.
Later. It stands. They stand, arm in arm. Four screws in Dev's hand. Insert, step 40: two figures hugging, four small screws.
Dev turns the last page. Insert, step 41: one figure alone, happy, on a new sofa. The figure has a bun.
Dev looks at the page. He looks up.
Noor is reading it very closely, with the smallest smile.

scripts.title: One More Taste
scripts.observation: The person ahead of you in the ice cream line tries every flavor while the line grows behind them.
scripts.caption_question: Can I try the pistachio?
scripts.new: tiny tasting spoons in a growing pile

beats.picture: The fox leans over the case, tiny spoon going in. The server already holding the next one. Bruno behind her.
Spoons pile on the counter.
lines: Can I try the mango? The other mango?

beats.picture: The line behind Bruno has grown: the goat, a rabbit, a raccoon, out of the door.
A hill of spoons. The server is grey with effort.
lines: Can I try the first one again?

beats.picture: Bruno, shaking slightly, very quiet.
The fox lifts one finger. The whole line leans in.
Silence. Bruno steps up to the case. The whole line breathes out.
Bruno studies the case. He picks one up with great care.
beats.sound: a distant groan from the line
